lexio

lexio is an R package for input-output models solved by preemptive (lexicographic) goal programming. You declare an input-output database (the technical structure, gross output, final demand, any number of satellite accounts and, optionally, a corridor on the economic deviations) and, for each account, a direction, a goal and a priority. The package chooses the sectoral output that best meets the goals in priority order,

G x + d⁻ − d⁺ = g,     G = [ D ; I − A ],     x, d⁺, d⁻ ≥ 0,

solving each priority level as a linear program with GLPK and locking the optima of the levels already solved. By default it runs every ordering of the priorities and reports every level of every run, in tables and in an Excel workbook.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("FilipeVascRocha/lexio")

On Linux, install GLPK first (for example, sudo apt install libglpk-dev). The file renv.lock records the versions of R and of every package used to develop and test the package; renv::restore() installs them.

Example 

library(lexio)

# a three-sector database with three satellite accounts and a corridor
io <- example_io()

# the entrant energy is a floor, the incumbent a ceiling, labour should grow 5%;
# the entrant gets a shock of 5% of the joint base of the two energy sources
model <- define_model(
  accounts = list(
    E   = list(direction = ">=", target = list(type = "pooled_share", share = 0.05, pool = c("E", "I"))),
    I   = list(direction = "<=", target = list(type = "base")),
    LAB = list(direction = ">=", target = list(type = "growth", rate = 0.05))
  )
)

res <- run_model(io, model)   # all 3! = 6 orderings, each with 4 priority levels
res
write_outputs(res, "results") # report, CSV tables and results.xlsx

Documentation

  • vignette("lexio"): get started, with a complete example.
  • vignette("model-specification"): declaring the data, the goals, the scenarios and the priorities; the outputs; the numerical behaviour.
  • vignette("miller-blair"): the goal programming example of Miller and Blair (2022), stage by stage.
  • vignette("thesis-replication"): the application to the Brazilian electricity and fuel markets.

The documentation is also available at https://filipevascrocha.github.io/lexio/, with Portuguese translations of the vignettes.

Replication of the thesis

The folder replication/ of the repository reproduces the results of the thesis that introduced the model (Rocha, 2026), from the 2018 Brazilian input-output matrix with energy-sector detail published by EPE. See its README.

Citation 

citation("lexio")

The package is archived on Zenodo. The DOI below covers all versions; each version also has its own DOI, listed on the Zenodo page, which pins the exact code you used:

Rocha, F. V. (2026). lexio: Generalized Input-Output Model with Preemptive Goal Programming (Version 1.0.1). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24293765

The model is described in:

Rocha, F. V. (2026). Modelo generalizado de insumo-produto com Goal Programming preemptivo aplicado à transição energética brasileira: eletricidade e combustíveis na estrutura produtiva de 2018. Doctoral thesis, Programa de Pós-graduação em Economia, Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora.

The database of the thesis, used in replication/:

Rocha, F. V. (2026). Database of the thesis, declared for the lexio package: Brazil, 2018 input-output matrix with energy-sector detail (fuels and electricity) (Version 1.0.0) [Dataset]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24293808
